result.title: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness
result.comment: Includes an appendix. Code available at https://github.com/tigranfah/ma-robustness
result.summary: A common occurrence in Large Language Models (LLMs) is the emergence of so-called massive activations. This phenomenon is well known in the literature and has been connected to attention sinks, representational compression, as well as signal propagation. However, the reasons and consequences for their appearance are not yet well understood. In this paper, we explain the role of massive activations in deep learning by showing that they are connected to the region migration phenomenon in delayed robustness. Under the spline theoretic interpretation of deep networks, we show that massive activations push the representations away from the nonlinearity boundaries of the network, decreasing the complexity of its input-output map around data points. Furthermore, we uncover for the first time that this phenomenon is not unique to transformers and actually appears in a number of common architectures performing simple supervised learning tasks. We validate this connection through extensive experiments on a diverse set of architectures including residual MLP, ResNet18, Vision Transformers and GPT and datasets including MNIST, CIFAR10, Imagenette and Shakespeare Text. We consistently observe that massive activations and region migration co-occur with adversarial robustness. Furthermore, we illustrate that this connection holds in the large-scale pretraining of LLMs by showing that the rise of massive activations in LLMs closely tracks the adversarial accuracy of the model under perturbations of the token embeddings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从对抗鲁棒性角度解释 massive activations 的作用，结合样条理论说明其将表示推离网络非线性边界、降低数据点附近的输入输出映射复杂度，并在 MLP、ResNet18、ViT、GPT 及多个数据集上验证其与 region migration 和对抗鲁棒性共现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其表示几何与局部复杂度分析可能启发对 VLM 内部视觉细节保留、latent 状态稳定性和 massive activation 干扰 latent 相似度的核查，但论文未研究多模态推理，联系仍较间接。
